# 1 Enoch Chapter 29 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 29 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 29:1 — "fragrant odors were raised up" vs. "rose up" vs. "filling the air"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fragrant odors were raised up from the trees" | Passive construction; literal |
| LOGOS | "fragrant odors rose up from these trees" | Active; more natural English |
| PNEUMA | "filling the air with the scent of resin and myrrh. Fragrant aromas rose up from them all around me" | Restructures sentence; adds "all around me" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "fragrant odors rose up from these trees." Active voice is more natural and the passive "were raised up" implies an agent unnecessarily. PNEUMA's "all around me" adds a first-person sensory note not in the Ge'ez.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 29:2 — "abundantly watered" valley and "Zit" plant

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "valley, which was abundantly watered" | Literal passive |
| LOGOS | "valley that was abundantly watered" | Relative clause; same meaning |
| PNEUMA | "richly watered" | "Richly" for "abundantly" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "abundantly watered." "Abundantly" is the standard English equivalent for the Ge'ez superlative; "richly" (PNEUMA) is acceptable but less precise. All three preserve "Zit" as the plant name.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Minor stylistic difference only.

---
